title: Etale localization preserves graded direct images and their evaluation counits
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $g:Y'\to Y$ be etale. Put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], with projections $h:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$. Use module direct images and tensor pullbacks on the small etale ringed topoi [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Let $(B_d)_{d\geq0}$ be $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with restriction-compatible bilinear products $B_m\otimes B_n\to B_{m+n}$ and unit $\mathcal O_X\to B_0$ satisfying associativity, ordinary commutativity, and the unit laws. All tensors are sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and all sums are coproducts of module sheaves. Set $C=\bigoplus_d f_*B_d$, $B'_d=h^*B_d$, and $C'=\bigoplus_d f'_*B'_d$, each with its homogeneous products of compatible sections. The canonical restriction isomorphisms $\beta_d:g^*f_*B_d\xrightarrow{\sim}f'_*h^*B_d$ identify both sides on an etale scheme $V\to Y'$ with the same compatible sections over $X\times_YV=X'\times_{Y'}V$. Their sum, through the canonical pullback/coproduct comparison, is an isomorphism of commutative unital graded algebras $\beta:g^*C\xrightarrow{\sim}C'$: $\beta_{m+n}(st)=\beta_m(s)\beta_n(t)$ and $\beta_0(1)=1$. Let $\epsilon_f:f^*C\to\bigoplus_d B_d$ and $\epsilon_{f'}:f'^*C'\to\bigoplus_d B'_d$ be the sums of the canonical module-adjunction counits. Under the canonical comparison $h^*f^*C\simeq f'^*g^*C$ and the pullback/coproduct comparisons, one has $h^*\epsilon_f=\epsilon_{f'}\circ f'^*\beta$. On a chart $W\to X'$ both sides send the local tensor $a\otimes s$ to $a\,s|_W$, also for sections with arbitrary local scalar coefficients. If $B_d=L^{\otimes d}$ for a line module $L$, the canonical tensor comparisons give $h^*B_d\simeq(h^*L)^{\otimes d}$ for all $d\geq0$, with $h^*\mathcal O_X\simeq\mathcal O_{X'}$ in degree zero; they preserve every homogeneous product and the unit, so the displayed algebra and evaluation comparisons use the actual tensor powers of the restricted line module.

source.place: Tag 03LX (lemma-pushforward-etale-base-change-modules), including the tensor-pullback footnote, applied to the homogeneous products and counits; spaces-descent.tex Tag 0D3C (lemma-descending-property-ample), proof: pullback compatibility of psi_d and their graded sum.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] to $F=B_d$ for each $d$. Its hypotheses are precisely the cartesian square and the etaleness of $g$; no quasi-compactness or quasi-coherence is needed. It identifies $g^*f_*B_d$ and $f'_*h^*B_d$ with the same compatible sections over $X\times_YV=X'\times_{Y'}V$, by the identity on every chart projection. These are the required $\beta_d$, natural in $B_d$ and in $V$. The same lemma identifies $h^*f^*G$ with $f'^*g^*G$ with the stipulated scalar-multiplication normalization.

For localization along $h$ or $g$, apply [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction] on each target scheme chart, where the localized site is the small etale site of its pullback. These comparisons agree on overlaps: both send every pure tensor of sections to the same pure tensor, so the uniqueness in [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] makes them equal. They therefore give the canonical tensor comparisons for $h^*$ and $g^*$. Their associativity and symmetry diagrams agree on $(s\otimes t)\otimes u$ and $s\otimes t$, respectively, hence agree as sheaf maps by the same uniqueness. By [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization], the structure ring is restricted with unchanged functions and the unit comparison is $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, with inverse $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. Thus these tensor comparisons also preserve the tensor unit.

source.place: Tags 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback) and 03DH (definition-localize-ringed-site); tensor universal property after Tag 0GMW

proof.text: Fix $m,n$ and an etale $V\to Y'$. Write compatible sections as families $(s_T)_T,(t_T)_T$ on charts of $X\times_YV$. Homogeneous multiplication in either direct image is the family $(\mu_{m,n}(s_T\otimes t_T))_T$. Step 1 leaves both families and every projection unchanged; Step 2 leaves the pure tensor unchanged. Consequently $\beta_{m+n}(st)=\beta_m(s)\beta_n(t)$. This equality on section pairings is equality of the maps from the sheaf tensor by [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal]. The unit section is the family of images of $1$ under $\mathcal O_X\to B_0$; the same calculation gives $\beta_0(1)=1$. Associativity, ordinary commutativity and the unit laws hold componentwise, since they hold in the given $B_d$. Equality of compatible families is detected by their chart projections [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors].

source.place: Tag 03LX, identity on restricted sections, applied to homogeneous pairings and unit

proof.text: Every tensor pullback under consideration is a left adjoint [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to the small discrete index category $\mathbf N$. In particular $g^*C\simeq\bigoplus_d g^*f_*B_d$. Compose this comparison with $\bigoplus_d\beta_d$; its inverse is the sum of the inverses. It respects the grading. Products of homogeneous summands and the degree-zero unit commute with it by Step 3, so the resulting $\beta$ is an isomorphism of unital commutative graded algebras. This is a coproduct argument in module sheaves, and makes no assertion that sections of an infinite coproduct are globally a direct sum of sections.

source.place: Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact (1), applied to the discrete category of nonnegative integers

proof.text: First compute a single counit $\epsilon_{f,F}:f^*f_*F\to F$. A chart tensor from $s\in(f_*F)(V)$ is $a\,\pi_{W,b}(\eta_{f_*F}(s))$ by [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Naturality of the chart projections gives its image under $\epsilon_{f,F}$ as $a\,\pi_{W,b}(f_*\epsilon_{f,F}(\eta_{f_*F}(s)))$. The adjunction triangle identity reduces this to $a\,\pi_{W,b}(s)=a\,s|_W$. The tensor realization [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] identifies these with actual local tensors, rather than just unit sections. Now set $F=B_d$. Step 1 fixes $s$ and its restrictions, and its pullback comparison multiplies scalar coefficients. Thus the two degree-$d$ paths in the asserted square both send $a\otimes s$ to $a\,s|_W$, for arbitrary $a$. They agree on finite sums by linearity, and on sheaf tensors by uniqueness of extension through sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. No global pure-tensor expression is required. Finally Step 4, also applied to $f^*,h^*,f'^*$, identifies the source and target coproducts; two maps from a coproduct are equal if their composites with every inclusion are equal. This proves $h^*\epsilon_f=\epsilon_{f'}\circ f'^*\beta$.

source.place: Tag 0D3C, lemma-descending-property-ample, paragraph on pullback of psi_d; explicit adjunction-triangle calculation supplied by the worker

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-canonical-etale-line-power-algebra] to L and its local rank-one hypothesis, obtaining A with canonical products. Apply the general graded restriction theorem (Steps 1--5 above) to A to obtain R. Apply [lem-trf-etale-line-power-comparison] to h, R.hh, A and R.restrictedAlgebra, using R.restrictedProducts to supply exactly the unchanged chart products and unit. This gives the actual power algebra A′, theta, its homogeneous algebra map and its first-power equation. For each d, naturality of the specified adjunction counit for f′ applied to (theta d).hom gives the last evaluation equation directly. This is CategoryTheory.Adjunction.counit_naturality, not an additional geometric compatibility assumption.

source.place: Tag 03EL, iterated with the tensor unit; spaces-descent.tex Tag 0D3C, the maps psi_d; final equality is adjunction counit naturality.
